niche: a county jail planning unit's 2027 forecast of felony probation revocation admissions, and the violator pods to staff, after a state act caps felony probation at 24 months, where probation officers meet a matter still open at a term's end with an extension when the term sits under its offense class's statutory maximum and with a violation petition when it does not
answer: Okelan County's 2027 Jail Operations Plan should staff 7 violator pods (448 beds) for felony probation revocation admissions (projection 1,424, 6.78 pods under the county's standard of one pod for each 210 admissions or part of 210)
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the two case systems, the Circuit Court's term orders and petitions, applies SB 26-118 to every felony term (each term's new end, no extension past 24 months) and builds the field's projection on two clocks, petitions by month on supervision and petitions in each term's last months before its expiration in force, at the record's own end-of-term rates with the extensions capped, files 911 admissions (five pods) against the golden's 1,424 (seven pods); persistence files 827 (four pods).
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the 2027 count of felony probation revocations, forecast from the supervision record the way the field forecasts failure on supervision (hazards by time on supervision and by time to the term's end, conversion of petitions to revocations, the filing-to-commitment lag), and it turns on probation law's two tools for a matter still open as a term runs out: the court may extend the term within its offense class's statutory maximum, and otherwise the officer files a violation petition so the court keeps jurisdiction. The Act's 24-month ceiling takes the extension away from every capped term, so their end-of-term petitions run at the rate of the terms already at their class maximum.

driver: At a term's end a unit with an open matter is extended where its term still has room under a ceiling and filed against where it has none, so the record's end-of-term failure rate is a mixture over units with and without room; a cap that takes the room from every capped unit moves all of them to the rate the units already at their ceiling show, and the pooled rate understates it by more than half.
driver_concrete: Okelan County's officers meet a matter still open at a felony term's end with an extension order when the term sits under its offense class's statutory maximum and with a violation petition when it does not; SB 26-118 bars any extension past 24 months, so every capped term (the 3,114 ending on 31 March 2027 and the rest at 24 months) files at the rate of the terms already at their class maximum, 38.7 per cent of terms reaching their last 120 days against the pooled 17.0 and 6.0 for terms with room.
stump: A competent solver builds the two-clock projection with the record's pooled end-of-term petition rate, caps the extensions under SB 26-118 and files 911 admissions (five pods); the step that lands it there is reading the end-of-term rate off terms that could mostly still be extended, when the Act leaves no capped term any room and the terms already at their class maximum show the rate such terms file at, so the plan staffs seven pods (1,424 projected).

differentiation.task152: task152 attributes a solar plant's decline at a module replacement to wear the replacement removes against dust it keeps; here nothing is replaced or decomposed: a legal option the statute removes moves every capped term onto the behaviour the terms that already lacked the option show.
differentiation.task141 v3: architecture 3's decisive step was the timing of the end-of-term petitions (the expiry clock), which both its readers took; here that clock is a lower rung, and the step is the rate the capped terms file at, taken from the terms already at their class maximum because the Act takes every capped term's extension room away.
differentiation.task253: task253 counts the units whose latent level sits below a fixed line from small, unequal samples, where shrinkage and the raw averages both miscount; here nothing is estimated per unit against a line: a legal option, an extension within the class maximum, is a precondition for the gentler outcome, and the statute removes it from every capped term at once, so the rate comes from the terms that already lacked it.
differentiation.task97: task97's architecture 4 converted a funded total into outcomes up to each category's eligible pool, a cap the closed years never exercised; here no pool caps anything: each term's end-of-term petition depends on whether the court can still extend it, and the record's terms at their class maximum already show the no-room behaviour the Act imposes on every capped term.

lineage.fate: spent, FAILED_TO_STUMP on the portal: both responses landed the call
lineage.driver: Outcomes are recorded only for the units a decision-maker let through, and the decision-makers, who sit by rota and so meet like caseloads, let through very different shares; a rule that lets every unit at a level through has to be priced at the rate the whole level would show, read from how outcomes per unit rise with each decision-maker's let-through share out to all let through, while any rate, model or reweighting fitted on the units already let through keeps the decision-makers' own selection and understates it.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a net figure whose offsetting term is provisioned in records filed under a different key, a different case and a category the decision's own eligibility rule excludes, so a pipeline that prices the decision on each unit's own record files a figure several times too large and inverts which levels are the cheapest to act on.
lineage.niche: a county jail's forward bed-day bill for the pretrial releases it already makes: how many detention bed-days the defendants released on a written promise at first appearance will cost the jail next year through the custody that follows a failure to appear, when that custody arrives under a new booking number on a new case on charges the release policy's own eligibility list excludes
lineage.stump: The analyst prices next year's releases at the bed-days of the released defendants' own short stays, projects that forward and files a figure about a quarter of the golden, because the custody that follows a failure to appear sits under new booking numbers on charges the eligibility list excludes and runs about 6 bed-days per failure at the lowest assessment score rising to about 19 at the highest.

lineage.driver: Failures are filed at two moments of each unit's term, early on and at a review held as the term lapses, so the failure rate by time since entry carries a spike at each term's own end; a cap that moves every term's end earlier moves the review with it and fires it at once for every unit already past the cap, while a forecast that truncates the time-since-entry curve at the cap drops the spike and files a fall.
lineage.niche: a county jail planning unit's 2027 forecast of felony probation revocation admissions, and the violator pods to staff, after a state act caps felony probation at 24 months and ends every longer running term on 31 March 2027, when probation officers file a violation petition in the weeks before a term lapses on cases with an unresolved matter so the court keeps jurisdiction
lineage.stump: A competent solver fits revocation by month on supervision with the risk score, carries it over each felony term's 2027 months to its end under SB 26-118 and files about 610 admissions (three pods); the step that lands it there is reading every petition on the time-since-start clock, when a quarter are filed in the last months before a term lapses, ride each term's scheduled end, and under the Act fire at once for the 3,373 terms that end on 31 March 2027, so the plan carries about 1,200 (six pods).
